subject: Dedicated GPU lane construct & trigger windows — NorthReach
messages:
From: Hiro Tanaka <hiro.tanaka@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena.morales@northreach.ai>, Procurement <procurement@northreach.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-12-05 09:15 -0800
Subject: Dedicated GPU lane construct & trigger windows — NorthReach

Hi Elena / NorthReach procurement team,

Thanks again for the conversation yesterday. Attached is a first-pass proposal for a dedicated GPU lane to support the NR production inference workload tied to the pilot and expected ramp. High-level asks below and a couple of options so you can pick what maps to your runway.

Summary (recommended starting configuration)
- Initial committed baseline: 8 GPUs (NVIDIA H100 or equivalent) as the "minimum active" for billing and warm-state availability.
- Canary / prewarm pool: 4 GPUs reserved for staging/canary traffic and for KV/prefix cache priming. These are billed as part of a warm-start buffer but can be fenced off from production for testing.
- Ramp schedule: incremental activations to reach 40 GPUs by month 6, driven by operational triggers (detailed below). Suggested cadence: +8 GPUs at months 1, 3, and 5 with smaller midpoints if utilization grows faster.
- Trigger-based step-ups: automatic allocation when 5-day moving average GPU utilization > 65% AND 95th-percentile tail latency > 250ms OR queue depth > 300 pending requests for 6+ hours.
- Autoscale headroom: allow 20% burst capacity beyond committed pool for short bursts (ephemeral GPUs) subject to availability.

Pricing & commercial notes
- Baseline commitment pricing attached in the PDF (NR-DedicatedProposal-v1.pdf).
- Introductory onboarding credit: 30 days of reduced unit price to offset KV cache warm-up and prompt engineering.
- We can structure a mid-term commit (16 GPUs for months 1–3) as a softened ramp if you prefer lower initial Opex.

Operational considerations
- Warm-start: We'll run a 72-hour KV cache priming job before traffic cutover to minimize early tail latency.
- Canary deploys: 4-GPU canary lane for model changes; automatic fallback to hosted variants if errors spike.
- Observability: token-level cost and per-route latency dashboards will be provisioned; we'll share read-only links for your SREs.

Next steps / asks
1) Confirm whether you want H100-class or A800-class nodes (costs differ; see proposal appendix).
2) Procurement timeline & PO cadence so we can reserve capacity windows.
3) Any security or SOC2 artifacts you need ahead of legal review.

I'm happy to jump on a quick 30-min follow up to walk through triggers and billing if helpful.

Thanks,
Hiro
Hiro Tanaka
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
hiro.tanaka@redwoodinference.com
Attachments: NR-DedicatedProposal-v1.pdf (PDF)

Subject: Re: Dedicated GPU lane construct & trigger windows — NorthReach

Thanks Hiro — this is very helpful. A few clarifying Qs from procurement and infra before we escalate to legal: 

1) Minimum active of 8 GPUs: can we see an alternate with a 4-GPU minimum for the first 60 days? Our finance team prefers lower committed floors for Q1.
2) Trigger thresholds: what are the operational risks of triggering on 5-day averages vs immediate spikes? Would we ever see oscillation that impacts cost predictability?
3) On pricing: can you confirm billing cadence (monthly in arrears vs upfront), and whether warm-start buffer GPUs are billed at full-rate?

Also need SOC2 Type II evidence and your standard DPA before we can sign. Can you attach those or point us to where they live?

We'd like to tentatively hold the capacity window for mid-Jan cutover pending answers.

—Elena
VP Product Operations | NorthReach
elena.morales@northreach.ai

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>

On 2026-12-05 09:15, Hiro Tanaka wrote:
> Attached is a first-pass proposal for a dedicated GPU lane...

Adding a few pragmatic options we should present to NorthReach to keep flexibility and help procurement sign-off quickly: 

Option A (Conservative, fastest approval)
- Start with 4 GPUs committed (billing min), 4 GPUs in canary/warm buffer (billed at 50% rate for first 30 days), option to convert to full 8 for month 2.
- Soft-commit ramp: convert additional 8 GPUs when 14-day moving average utilization > 60% for two consecutive weeks.
- Discount: 10% on unit price for first 3 months if they commit to a 6-month window.

Option B (Recommended for stability)
- Baseline 8 GPUs committed + 4 GPU canary. Trigger-based steps to 40 as Hiro outlined.
- Provide a 45-day onboarding credit (applied as one-time invoice credit) to offset warm-up costs.
- Discount: 6% for 12-month rolling commitment.

Operational notes for our SREs to include in the offer
- Pre-warm automation: run job to populate runtime KV cache and sample prompts to precompute embeddings.
- Canary rollback policy: automatic rollback if model error-rate > 1.5% or latency delta > 40% vs baseline.

Commercial ask to Marissa: can we approve the 10% intro discount on Option A to help close faster? If not, we'll propose the 6% alternative in the external doc.

-Karthik
Director, Sales Engineering | Redwood Inference

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena.morales@northreach.ai>, Hiro Tanaka <hiro.tanaka@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: Dedicated GPU lane construct & trigger windows — NorthReach

Elena — quick operational detailset from the infra/onboarding perspective.

Thanks for flagging the 4 GPU min ask; technically feasible with a phased runbook. Practical notes: 
- Canary gating: we recommend a 72-hour warm window and a rolling traffic split (5% -> 25% -> 100%) over 48 hours for major model changes.
- Trigger tuning: use a dual-condition policy (5-day avg utilization + 12-hour sustained queue depth) to avoid oscillation. Example: step-up triggers when 5-day avg GPU usage > 65% AND 12-hour sustained queue depth > 200. Downscaling should be manual for first 90 days.
- KV priming job: will take ~18-36 hours depending on corpus; plan one maintenance window to run at low traffic.

I've attached a short onboarding-runbook.md stub and included suggested SLA guardrails in the doc. Also note that ephemeral burst capacity is subject to availability — if they need hard guaranteed buffer, we should convert to committed GPUs (more predictable but higher cost).

Operational readiness checklist (short)
- Confirm model artifact sizes and KV corpus size
- Agree on cutover weekend and blackout windows
- Provide SOC2/DPA request list to legal (we will attach these when pushing to the docs package)

Happy to run a walkthrough with NorthReach infra next week.

-Priyom
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
Attachments: onboarding-runbook.md (text)
